original_record.question:
A right circular cone is inscribed in a right circular cylinder. The volume of the cylinder is $72\pi$ cubic centimeters. What is the number of cubic centimeters in the space inside the cylinder but outside the cone? Express your answer in terms of $\pi$.

<image1>
original_record.solution: A cylinder with radius $r$ and height $h$ has volume $\pi r^2 h$; a cone with the same height and radius has volume $(1/3)\pi r^2 h$.  Thus we see the cone has $1/3$ the volume of the cylinder, so the space between the cylinder and cone has $2/3$ the volume of the cylinder, which is $(2/3)(72\pi) = \boxed{48\pi}$.
